coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Federal (Supply Control Act 1961, KPDN). No monthly-report duty confirmed. BUDI95 MyKad verification is a state-run digital system (3.1m transactions/day; PDAM backs strict SOP; manual book only as outage fallback). Nothing for a vendor beyond a weak station-side audit book idea. LPG: unlicensed-storage enforcement only.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: MPOB licence categories (DF palm fruit dealers, MF mills): payment vouchers and purchase statements are licence conditions, and SIMS is a mandatory licence condition with enforcement notices (state tool likely covers the core job). Rice is K05 (not re-checked). Nothing else reached for coffee or cocoa.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Strong signal. SKM data (Dec 2024): 16,009 co-operatives, 9,823 active, 7,779 failed to maintain accounts, 2,304 not audited. SKM audit/accounting grants RM3,000 (Peninsular) and RM3,500 (Sabah/Sarawak). Feb 2026 ministry warning: poor performers face funding freeze or legal action. Existing tools: free p-SKM Excel (2014-15) and commercial SPBK (MOCCIS).

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Act 586 amendment is only under study (billing and price control), licensing guideline dated 17 Oct 2025, prosecutions of unregistered clinics. GP/TPA claims is K09 (rejected). AELB X-ray licensing for clinics: law identified (Act 304, Radiation Protection Officer) but renewal and reporting duties unverified.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Poisons Regulations amendment (Parliament paper ST.164/2025): pharmacist engagement and attendance records (Forms D/E), registers kept 5 years, fines up to RM5,000. Poisons Act 2022 amendment allows fully digital records. Price marking is K14 (rejected). Medical device importers need an MDA establishment licence plus GDPMD certificate; no annual filing found. Controlled-chemical users (DOSH chemical register, precursors) not reached.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security agencies: licence under Private Agencies Act 1971 (KDN/MOHA), renewal before 31 Dec each year, audited accounts and company papers at year-end (2007 circular and 2020 Parliament reply, old), guard quotas, only Malaysians and screened Nepalese permitted. Amendment is only an association (PIKM) proposal. Cleaning and manpower/outsourcing agencies not reached.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: CIDB Act 520: contractor registration (K16 renewal rejected), project declaration and levy (1,359 compounds in 2023), mandatory registration of construction workers (green card), Sarawak joint operations 2025. No Act 520 amendment found. Quarry and river-sand: state mineral enactments differ by state; no reporting duty confirmed, nothing found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: AMLA (Amendment) Act 2025 in force 1 Mar 2026 (52 sections, individual liability); BNM AML/CFT/CPF Newsletter 01/2026 reports directive orders to estate agents, lawyers, company secretaries and dealers in precious metals/stones. DNFBP Sector 5 covers lawyers, accountants, company secretaries, REAs, moneylenders, pawnbrokers. Gold shops are K06. Law-firm client-account reports and estate-agent firm returns not reached.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Penang Private Short-term Accommodation By-Laws 2026 effective 1 Aug 2026, application before enforcement on 1 Nov 2026, about 6,000 units (MySTRA estimate), licence from MBPP/MBSP. National: MOTAC says STRA operators will need PBT business licence before TAP registration; Tourism Industry Act amendments proposed; PLANMalaysia guidelines pending. Perak Hotel Regulations 2024 homestay fee RM200. Guest-register and tourism-tax rules for hosts not found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Palm: National Traceability System (SIMS + GeoSawit + e-MSPO), MSPO about 90% estates and 85% independent smallholders, MPOB funds smallholder certification. EUDR smallholder deadline push to Dec 2027 requested, not settled. Rubber/cocoa/small collector duties unverified. Edible bird's nest is the strongest find (see 31). Fish catch certificates and timber not reached.

coverage.category: 31. Edible bird's nest (swiftlet) farms, processors and exporters
coverage.found: More than 15,000 swiftlet farms in the official traceability system (Bernama opinion piece); new Malaysia-China protocol signed 13 Nov 2025 replacing 2012 and 2016 ones; exports suspended Dec 2024 and resumed Jan 2025; DVS VHM/GVHP processor certification. Farm-level licensing and records duties unverified.

coverage.category: 32. Tobacco and vape retailers (Act 852, Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024)
coverage.found: Display ban and product registration enforcement from 1 Oct 2025; online and vending sales banned; vape retail licences are decided by states/PBTs (Johor, Terengganu, Perlis, Pahang, Kelantan and Kedah refuse). No retailer register or software angle found.

coverage.category: 33. Licensed moneylenders (Moneylenders Act 1951, Act 400)
coverage.found: KPKT requires electronic fund transfer for loan payouts since 1 Apr 2024; KPKT piloting a borrower/moneylender data repository (late 2025 proposal); Consumer Credit Act 2025 passed July 2025 with a Consumer Credit Commission planned for 2028. No Act 400 amendment found. Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan licence separately.

coverage.category: 34. SST expansion from 1 July 2025 (rental/leasing, F&B, private healthcare, others)
coverage.found: Thresholds: rental/leasing and financial services RM1m, F&B RM1.5m, private healthcare RM1.5m, otherwise RM500k; returns via MySST (SST-02, bimonthly); manual return relief for Jul-Sep 2025; penalty-free period reported ended 31 Dec 2025 (third-party source). Generic tax filing, so mostly out of scope.

coverage.category: 35. Childcare (taska, Act 308) and elderly care centres (Act 506 / Act 802)
coverage.found: Taska must register with JKM; registration plaque mandatory from 1 Jan 2026 (ministerial announcement); 4,016 registered taska; Act 802 (private elderly health care) gazetted 2018 but not enforced; Act 308 amendment delayed. Overlaps group A category 20.

coverage.category: 36. Sabah and Sarawak differences (Sarawak State Sales Tax and state rules)
coverage.found: Sarawak State Sales Tax is narrow (petroleum, tyres, new vehicles, 1.5% on ferroalloy/polysilicon exports from 1 Sep 2024); federal SST applies in Sarawak too. Sabah/Sarawak co-operatives get a higher SKM grant. Sabah smallholder intermediaries flagged as an EUDR traceability weakness (EFI).

coverage.category: 37. Medical device establishments (Act 737, MDA)
coverage.found: Importers/distributors need an establishment licence plus GDPMD certificate; retailers excluded; MDA joined MDSAP in Sept 2025. No annual filing duty found for small distributors. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 38. River sand, quarry and mineral dealers (state mineral enactments)
coverage.found: No reporting duty or software angle confirmed. Rules are state enactments (for example Selangor Circular 2/2025 on selling state minerals, Perak penalties up to RM250,000), so any product would have to be built state by state.
